apropos.chapo: A beekeeping management information system, built for the apiary as much as for the desk.

sections.texte: Livestock, apiary visits, sensors, harvests and batch traceability in a single application. It exists so you can tell how the colonies are doing without cross-checking three notebooks.
Beekeeping holdings and the people who work the livestock. You come in by invitation, with a role that decides what you see and what you may change.
The interface exists in French, English and Arabic. Arabic is not merely translated: the layout is genuinely mirrored, from the navigation to the tables.
The application installs like a phone app and stays usable with no network. A visit recorded at the apiary waits on the device and leaves at synchronisation, when the connection returns.

sections.texte: Zümm is a beekeeping management and monitoring software: livestock, apiary visits, sensors, harvests and batches. These terms describe the expected use of the service by the members of a holding.
There is no open sign-up. Creating an account requires a holding code, issued by the manager of the holding you are joining. That code also determines the role you are given on arrival.

Four human roles exist: beekeeper, supervisor, manager and administrator. They decide what each person may read and change. A fifth role is reserved for sensor gateways: it can only submit measurements.
It must be at least twelve characters long, and it is personal to you. Creations, changes and deletions made with your account are written to the audit log under your name.

The service is used with the role you were given. Circumventing access controls, or extracting apiary locations in bulk, falls outside that use: the coordinates of an apiary carry a market value far beyond that of the software.

The application stays usable at the apiary with no network. Until an entry has been synchronised it exists only on the device that captured it: clearing the browser data before synchronisation loses it.

The software evolves and screens may change. The guaranteed level of availability, the termination terms and what becomes of the data at the end of the contract are matters for the organisation putting Zümm online.

sections.texte: It describes the data the software processes as it is written in its code: the categories come from its tables, the recipients from its only outbound calls. What depends on the operating organisation — its identity, the periods it applies — is not covered here.

This is the most sensitive data in the product, and not primarily for privacy reasons: the coordinates of an apiary are worth a stolen stock of hives. They never leave as they are. A server-side filter blurs or removes them according to the role of whoever asks, and every new screen carrying coordinates goes through it.

Each holding only sees its own data. The separation is not applied by the interface but by the database itself, on every request: a programming mistake in one screen cannot let another holding's data out.
No authentication token is kept in the browser. The session lives in a cookie only the server can read, and the server renews it. Ending the session revokes it server-side, not only in the tab.
Creations, changes and deletions are written to a log: who, what, when. It can be read by the holding manager and the administrator, and it cannot be altered.

No automatic purge is programmed in the software: what is entered stays until the operator deletes it. The periods actually applied are therefore theirs, and are among the items to be completed above.

Access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability and objection are exercised with the data controller. The application already exports visits and hives as CSV or text from the matching screens; for anything else, the request goes through the manager of your holding.

ressources.chapo: The questions that keep coming back, answered by describing the application as it actually works.

questions.q: How do I get an account?
questions.r: There is no open sign-up. Ask the manager of your holding for a holding code, then enter it in the “Create an account” tab of the sign-in screen. That code also determines the role you are given.
Passwords are handled by the authentication service, not by Zümm. Go through the manager of your holding: they are the one who can restart the procedure.

questions.q: Can I work with no network at the apiary?
questions.r: Yes. The application installs like a phone app and stays usable offline. Your entries wait on the device and leave at synchronisation; a counter at the top of the screen shows how many are still pending.

questions.q: Why can I not see the Audit screen?
questions.r: Because your role does not open it: the audit log and the invitations are reserved for the manager and the administrator. It is not a failure and there is nothing to retry — ask your manager for a role change.

questions.q: Who can see the exact location of my apiaries?
questions.r: Coordinates come out filtered according to the role of whoever asks, and are never returned as they are to everyone. The filter is applied by the server, not by the interface: working around it from a browser yields nothing.

questions.q: How do I export my data?
questions.r: Visits and hives export as CSV or text from their own screens. For anything else, the request goes through the manager of your holding.
Into French, English and Arabic. Arabic is written right to left: the layout is genuinely mirrored, not merely translated.

sections.titre: Why there is no “forgotten password” link
sections.texte: Because it would send nothing. Password reset by email is a function of the authentication service, and no mail server is configured there: the link would exist, the message would not leave.
Zümm does not store your password and cannot remind you of it. A reset creates a new one; the old one is readable by nobody, not even your manager.
An account you cannot reach does not lock the livestock: the data belongs to the holding, not to your account, and the other agents reach it according to their role.

permissions.sousTitre: Who may do what. The server is the authority — this page describes what it applies.
permissions.intro: The interface hides what it knows to be closed, but it decides nothing: every call is checked by the server. A valid token without a business role reaches no endpoint.

regles.referentiel: Creating, changing or deleting in the reference data: farmers, farms, apiaries, agents, hives
regles.reste: Everything else: consultation, and recording field work

permissions.ecransTexte: For the roles that do not open them, these screens appear neither in the rail nor in the palette: {ecrans}.
permissions.note: Hiding is a navigation convenience, not a protection. What the browser hides, it could show — it is the server that refuses.

introuvable.explication: This address matches no screen of the console. The link may be incomplete or outdated.

interdit.explication: Your account is signed in, but its role does not open this screen. Nothing failed: there is simply nothing to retry here.
interdit.rolesRequis: This screen is restricted to the following roles: {roles}. The manager of your holding can change yours.

panne.explication: The server is not responding as it should. Your input is not at fault. Try again in a moment; if it persists, tell the manager of your holding.

tournee.aucune: No visit planned on that day.
tournee.avertissement: Indicative order: straight-line distances, non-optimal heuristic. Not a road itinerary.
tournee.simulee: Order changed on this screen only: nothing is saved, and distances become estimates.

emplacements.aide: Moving the apiary closes the current location and opens a new one. To fix a mistyped position, edit the record instead.

transports.aide: Carrying out a move relocates the apiary: the current location closes and a new one opens, exactly as a direct move would.

abonnements.aide: A URL your calendar (Google, Outlook, Apple) re-reads on its own. Treat it as a password: don't share it, and revoke it when you change device.
abonnements.urlUnique: This URL is shown once. Copy it now — it cannot be retrieved later.

indice.aide: Computed on each read from inspection observations, never stored. With no recent observation, no index is shown — a gauge over nothing would pass ignorance off as a diagnosis.

carence.bloquee: This hive is within a withdrawal period: its honey cannot be harvested.
carence.aide: You may override, but the decision goes to the audit log with your reason. An override without an explanation is worthless during an inspection.

lectures.variance_nulle: Constant value: no coefficient can be computed

correlation.avertissement: A correlation is not a cause: two warm months coinciding with an acacia flow do not prove that heat makes honey.

rucher.aide: The average covers only colonies actually assessed: counting an unvisited colony as zero would sink an apiary nobody has seen yet.

comparaison.aide: No overall score: mixing kilos, plant species and altitude would give a number with the authority of a measurement and none of its substance. The criteria stay side by side.

equipe.aide: These figures help spread a workload, never compare people: ten overdue tasks usually means three days of rain.

horsLigne.aide: A download is dated: the console shows when it was taken every time it is read, so disk data never passes for fresh data. No sensor readings and no weather — they go stale too fast.
horsLigne.emportImpossible: Taking an apiary offline needs the network: do it before you leave.
horsLigne.perime: taken {jours} days ago — too old to be read
horsLigne.refusAide: The server refused these entries when syncing — usually because another beekeeper got there first. Nothing is lost: the call is yours.
horsLigne.brouillonsAide: An entry started at the apiary can be finished at home. A draft belongs to its beekeeper: nobody else reads it, not even a manager.
horsLigne.economieAide: Turns off the map background (WebGL), background refreshes and animations. Nothing switches on by itself: an app that changes behaviour silently looks broken.
horsLigne.installerAide: Once installed, the console starts without a network. Do it before heading out.
horsLigne.installationManuelle: On this browser, use the share menu: “Add to Home Screen”.
horsLigne.dejaInstallee: App already installed on this device.
horsLigne.noteVocaleAide: The note stays on this device: the server stores no audio file. It is there to help you type up on return, then it is deleted.
horsLigne.noteVocaleImpossible: The microphone is not available on this device.

etiquettes.aide: The short code is the hive's identifier: it can be read by eye when the QR is dirty, wet or propolised. The NFC tag carries exactly the same thing.
etiquettes.plancheAide: One label per hive in the chosen apiary. Printing outputs the sheet only, not the console around it.
etiquettes.nfcApprochez: Hold the tag against the device…
etiquettes.nfcEchec: NFC write failed: tag too far, write-protected, or permission denied.
etiquettes.nfcIndisponible: NFC is not available in this browser — it exists on neither iOS nor Firefox. The QR code stays the baseline; the tag is a convenience.

interfaceProgressive.aide: The essential interface hides the screens a three-hive beekeeper has no use for: sensors, packing batches, swarms, queens, audit log. It removes no rights — a direct link still works, and the setting changes back in one click.

demonstration.aide: Loads a fictional operation — one farmer, one farm, one beekeeper, two apiaries, five hives and their visits — so you can walk the console with data in it. Everything loaded is tracked, and removal deletes only that: never something you entered yourself, even if it shares the name.
demonstration.indisponible: The demo dataset is disabled on this deployment.
demonstration.confirmation: Remove the demo dataset and the {objets} objects it created?

etage.aide: This weight answers a different question from the scale: not how much the hive weighs, but where the honey is. It feeds neither threshold alerts nor the harvest forecast — adding up weighings taken at different times would give a weight that never existed.

partage.aide: Shows ONE hive's curve to someone outside the operation — a mentor, a bee inspector, an association. They see a curve and a label: no identifier, no apiary, no location. The link expires, can be revoked, and its last use is visible.
partage.urlUnique: Copy this link now: it will never be shown again.

materiel.aidePeriodicite: An empty interval means “needs no servicing” — an empty super, say — not “service it whenever”: nothing will be proposed for this item.

stock.aide: Stock without a threshold is an inventory: it says what you have, never what you lack. The threshold is what raises “reorder”.
stock.aideSeuil: Hitting the threshold exactly is already being short: the comparison is inclusive.

depense.aideAffectation: Assignment is optional: a bought queen belongs to a hive, transport to an apiary, insurance to nothing at all. Requiring one would invent assignments, and per-hive profitability would become false.

bilan.aide: Income is a VALUATION of honey production at the configured price, not turnover: Zümm does not know your selling prices. The period is asked for, never guessed.
bilan.nonAffectees: Including €{montant} not assigned to any hive — not distributed: insurance does not divide by the number of colonies.

saison.aide: Dashboards work on a rolling period — twelve months receding every day. These are calendar years, and the yield counts the hives that produced, not those that existed.

exportIntegral.aide: Fourteen resources, three formats. Sensor readings are capped at the last ninety days, and the apiary export carries no coordinates — a file travels, and it has no role attached.

carnet.aucunPoint: No extra point: the standard grid only.
carnet.aucunGabarit: No template yet. The standard grid applies.
carnet.confirmationSuppression: Delete template “{nom}”? Recorded visits keep their observations.
carnet.aide: The catalogue is closed: you switch existing boxes on, you never invent new ones. That is what keeps observations comparable between apiaries and across years.
carnet.noyauAide: Switching a section off hides it from the form; nothing already recorded is erased.
carnet.statistiquesAide: The denominator is how many times the point was actually CHECKED, never the number of visits: a quick visit that ticked nothing does not count.

refractometre.aide: Above 18 % water, honey ferments in the jar; above 20 %, it falls outside the standard. The instrument must be calibrated, and the value entered must be the index it displays.
refractometre.horsTable: Outside the published table: nothing is extrapolated.

elevage.ligneeDescription: Lineage tree: mothers above, daughters below, the selected queen in the centre.
elevage.serieAide: Counts are entered as the days pass: acceptance at five days, emergence at twelve, mating three weeks later. They are not derived from the recorded queens — only the ones kept get recorded, and the rate would be wrong, always too low.
elevage.pasDeRuche: This queen is not in a hive: nothing can be observed of her.
elevage.indexAide: No overall score is computed, and none should be: gentleness, an infestation rate and kilograms do not add up. Each criterion is in its own unit, with the number of observations behind it.

dictee.relecture: Dictated text is reviewed before it is saved.
dictee.refusDistante: This browser would send your voice to a recognition service, so dictation is disabled. It works where transcription happens on the device.

briefing.aide: This briefing is computed from your own records — alerts, tasks, withdrawal periods, last visits. No language model is involved: every line cites what it rests on, and can be checked in one click.

modeLocal.aide: Two separate halves, each set on its own: the server cuts weather and the anomaly microservice; this device cuts map tiles, which are fetched by your browser and reveal where your apiaries are. Anomaly detection keeps working — it then runs right here.
modeLocal.carteCoupee: Map tiles disabled by local mode.

bluetooth.absent: This browser does not expose Bluetooth (Safari on iPhone and Firefox do not). The gateway remains everyone's path.
bluetooth.profil: Zümm speaks the standard Bluetooth profile — temperature, humidity, battery. A sensor that departs from it needs its own adapter, which we will not write without the device at hand.
bluetooth.rien: This sensor exposes none of the expected readings.

antivol.aide: A sudden weight drop that no harvest explains raises an alert. It does not close by itself: a stolen hive does not come back, and an alert that vanished because the scale is lying on the ground would be worse than no alert.
